judgments.reasoning_cat1: The granting language is standard, but it is riddled with OCR/typing slips ('parcel!', 'made apart hereof', 'any and ail') and describes the land only as 'approximately 10.89 acres' subject to Exhibit A. Nothing in it names a term with two genuine competing meanings, so the intrinsic risk is modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against §3 (deed to contain 'new legal descriptions' reflecting the plat of vacation of Sixth and Abbott Streets) and §5 (updated plat of survey) and the attachment list ('Exhibit A — Legal Description (2)'): the parcel conveyed here may not match the post-vacation descriptions those sections require. That is a real but secondary tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The price mechanics are internally garbled: 'less any deductions identified below' and 'or less dependent upon setoffs as described below' point to deductions and setoffs that are never in fact identified below, and $8,000,000 plus a $1,000,000 'Outstanding Balance' payable only out of 10% of TIF receipts leaves it uncertain whether the balance is ever unconditionally owed. Named vague/undefined terms — 'standard deductions', 'setoffs as described below', 'outstanding incurred eligible expenses' — make this the most construable clause in the instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §28 repeats the last sentence but says 'less any setoff' where §2 says 'less any deductions', and §9 (Prorations) covers taxes and charges that §2 also purports to prorate; nothing anywhere defines the deductions/setoffs referenced. The mismatch with §28 and the missing setoff provision is a concrete whole-instrument incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Permitted Exceptions' is defined by reference to a Real Estate Option Agreement whose date is left blank, and the clause simultaneously promises title 'free from any and all liens or encumbrances' and 'subject only to' those exceptions. The blank date and the reliance on an extrinsic instrument to fix the defined term are namable defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §4 speaks of 'Permitted Exceptions attached hereto' and the attachment list has 'Exhibit B — Permitted Exceptions', so the definition here (option agreement) and the definition in §4/Exhibit B are two different sources for one defined term. That is a specific cross-provision inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause contains blanks ('the office in ___'), a typo ('expanse' for expense), and an odd cure window — Seller 'shall have ten (10) business days prior to the date of Closing' is ambiguous between a ten-day period and a deadline ten days before Closing. Buyer's election must be made 'prior to the expiration of the period for Seller to remedy', which compounds the timing uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to Permitted Exceptions 'attached hereto', while §3 defines them by reference to the Option Agreement; and its 30-day/10-business-day scheme must fit the 90-day outside Closing date in §8(a) and the 'time is of the essence' rule in §17. The definitional clash with §3 is specific.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and largely mechanical, though it sets no delivery deadline ('Provided this agreement shall have been executed') and contains a garbled phrase ('as a prepared in accordance'). Nothing here has two competing commercial meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against §3 (deed with post-vacation legal descriptions) and §8(a) (90-day Closing): the survey depends on the City's final approved plat of vacation, an event no provision makes a condition or assigns responsibility for, but no direct contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The as-is acceptance is broad and carries its own carve-out — 'except as expressly set forth elsewhere in the Agreement' — whose reach is left open, and it makes Buyer accept 'all faults... whether latent or patent and whether now or hereafter existing'. The unbounded carve-out is a namable source of dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against §7(b)–(e) (affirmative environmental and title representations), §11 (Seller bears risk of loss and must repair injury beyond ordinary wear and tear before delivery of the deed) and §23 (representations survive Closing); acceptance of the Property 'in the condition existing on the date of closing' is hard to reconcile with §11's repair obligation. That is a concrete conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare introductory lead-in with nothing operative beyond 'covenants and represents'. No term to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in §6 or §23 contradicts a mere introduction to the representations. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain record-ownership and authority representation with no vague or double-meaning term. Standard drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against §24 (which contemplates the Option assigned by GSA and requires the Government's signature to amend) — Seller's ownership representation is consistent with the recited structure. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Knowledge qualifiers here are uneven — 'no knowledge of any reason' (typed 'teason') as to development, 'to its knowledge' as to title — and 'would not allow the Property to be developed for the Federal Office facilities contemplated herein' is vague about what approvals are covered. The mixed qualifiers and the typo are namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Compared with §7(e)'s 'to the best of Seller's actual knowledge' standard and §13's contemplated use 'as a leasehold for Federal facilities', the knowledge standards differ across the same representation set but do not squarely contradict. Moderate-low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The qualifier 'for its current use' materially narrows the utility representation for a buyer planning a new federal facility, and 'sufficient size, capacity' is undefined. That qualifier is a specific, arguable limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §26 repeats this representation almost verbatim but adds 'Gas', drops 'for its current use', and then makes all utility relocations Buyer's sole cost — a direct textual divergence between two representations about the same subject. That is a named conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The disclosure is concrete (statutory 'facility' status, asbestos, environmental reports) and 'all environmental information that it has' is self-limiting. Little to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with §6 (Buyer accepts all faults, latent or patent) and §7(e) (exceptions 'as described in paragraph 7(d)'), the disclosure is carved out of the environmental representations coherently. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sub-item (3) is convoluted — it conditions the absence of liability-triggering 'activities' on a subsequent purchaser 'avail[ing] itself of the available statutory exemptions', which is a strange condition on a representation — and the 'to the best of Seller's actual knowledge' qualifier reaches all three items ambiguously. The stray dash in '(1) —' shows the transcription is imperfect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It excepts matters 'indicated on Schedule A attached', but the attachment list at the end names only Exhibit A and Exhibit B — no Schedule A exists in the instrument. That missing schedule is a specific whole-instrument gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'will continue to be true and correct on each day hereafter' is unbounded in time and unqualified, which is odd for representations made 'to the best of Seller's actual knowledge'. The open-ended temporal reach is namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against §7(e)'s knowledge qualifier and §23 (No Merger — representations survive until improvements are completed and occupancy accepted): this sentence strips the knowledge qualifiers and gives no end date, while §23 supplies one. That tension is real if secondary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumeration is broken — '(i) (ii) (iii) (iv)' appear as empty placeholders before the text, so the numbering of the closing obligations does not line up with the paragraphs that follow. 'Mutually agreeable date, but in no event later than ninety (90) days' is otherwise definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mislabeled subparagraphs matter because §8(a)(iv) refers to itself as 'This Section 8(a)(v)' while possession is separately numbered (v), and §17 makes time of the essence against a 'mutually agreeable date'. The numbering incoherence is concrete but low-stakes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short deed-delivery obligation cross-referencing §3; 'any exceptions created or suffered by Buyer' is mildly open but conventional. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-checked with §3 (warranty deed, Permitted Exceptions defined by the Option Agreement) and §4 (Exhibit B): the added carve-out for Buyer-created exceptions is consistent with both. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A FIRPTA certification tied to a statutory definition; the terms are defined by reference to Section 1445. Essentially nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses tax withholding or transferor status, so there is nothing to conflict with. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It misidentifies itself ('This Section 8(a)(v)') when possession is the (v) item, omits a word ('if required the Title Company'), and limits the duty by the undefined phrase 'extraordinary obligations'. Both a mechanical error and a vague term are namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against §18 (Possession) which is the actual (v), and §4 (title policy issuance) and §16 (Other Acts, 'reasonably necessary' further assurances): the self-reference is wrong and this clause overlaps §16 without a priority rule. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, passive but unmistakable in meaning; no timing or condition is stated, but delivery 'at Closing' is supplied by the lead-in. Very little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with §8(a) (obligations at Closing) and §13 (pre-closing entry rights subject to Seller's uses), possession at Closing is consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional escrow-closing mechanic with a clear 50/50 fee split; 'undertakings... necessary for the Closing in escrow' is mildly open but routine. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against §4 (Seller pays the title commitment cost 'at Sellers sole cost') and §8(a)(iv) (Title Company documentation): the 50% escrow-fee split does not contradict Seller's sole responsibility for the title commitment. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All real estate taxes, expenses and charges in connection with ownership and use of the Property' is a broad catch-all with no enumerated carve-outs, so its reach is somewhat open. Otherwise mechanically sound.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §2 already describes 'standard deductions and prorations (customary closing expenses... inclusive of utility and real estate tax prorations)' and §26 makes utility relocation costs Buyer's alone; the overlap between §2, §9 and §26 leaves the allocation of utility charges arguable. Moderate-low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Buyer-default remedy is self-contradictory: Seller gets 'liquidated damages not to exceed $50,000' in the form of a letter of credit, yet the last sentence adds that 'the parties may seek any other remedy available at law or in equity', which negates the liquidated-damages cap; 'fetter of credit' is a further typo. The escrow trigger ('upon the execution of this Agreement and within ten (10) business days of Award and Assignment of the Option to Purchase') states two inconsistent times and refers to 'Any subsequent Buyer' with no defined meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against §24 (the Option assigned to Buyer) and §17 (time of the essence): nothing elsewhere defines 'Award and Assignment of the Option to Purchase' or the 'subsequent Buyer', and the general remedies sentence undercuts the specific-performance/actual-damages menu given for Seller default in the same section. That combination is a genuine internal incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Injury beyond the ordinary wear and tear' is a vague threshold, and the Seller's election to 'repair the damage... or make an appropriate deduction from the purchase price' leaves 'appropriate' unquantified and the choice unallocated. Both are namable vagueness points.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely contradicts §6, under which Buyer 'agrees to accept the Property in the condition existing on the date of closing of title, including all faults... whether now or hereafter existing'; it also sits against §12, which forbids any Purchase Price reduction for condemnation takings. That is a specific conflict with two named provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Substantial' is defined circularly as a portion that 'would impair or otherwise affect the intended use' — 'otherwise affect' would make almost any taking substantial — and the first sentence is a fragment ending in a period before 'Buyer shall have the right'. It also uses 'Real Property', a term the Agreement never defines (the defined term is 'Property').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against §11 (Seller bears risk of loss until deed delivery and may reduce the price) and §1 (Seller assigns condemnation-type awards to Buyer at closing), the allocation of awards on termination to Seller and the 'no reduction in the Purchase Price' rule are in some tension but not flatly contradictory. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is written in the vocabulary of a different instrument — 'the period of this Option including any extension periods', 'Optionee', 'Optionor' — none of which are defined here, so who owes the insurance, repair and notice duties is uncertain on the face of the text. 'Any other due diligence matters deemed reasonably prudent' is also an open-ended catch-all after a specific list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is a purchase agreement with a 90-day Closing under §8(a); there is no 'Option' period in it (§24 merely recites the assigned Real Estate Option Agreement), so the entry right has no ascertainable term within this instrument. That is a concrete whole-instrument incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Buyer's notice address is left entirely blank, and the deemed-receipt sentence covers mail and courier but omits the personal-delivery method it authorises. Both are mechanical gaps that affect when notice is effective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Notice timing drives the five-day default cure in §10, the ten-day condemnation election in §12 and the termination election in §4, so the missing address and missing personal-delivery rule ripple outward, though no provision contradicts this one. Moderate-low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No commission or other amount is payable to any other person or entity' uses 'other' without an antecedent — no broker is named — so it is unclear whether the parties are excluding all brokers or all brokers besides some unstated one. A small but namable slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision mentions brokers or commissions, so there is nothing in the instrument to contradict it. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional further-assurances covenant limited by 'reasonably necessary'; boilerplate of this kind rarely supports competing readings. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps §8(a)(iv), which imposes a similar duty and expressly excludes 'extraordinary obligations', but the two are readily harmonised. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard time-of-the-essence language with an ordinary weekend/holiday extension; nothing in it carries two meanings. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against §8(a) ('a mutually agreeable date' for Closing) and §2 (post-closing TIF payments running for years): making time of the essence for 'every provision hereof in which time is an element' fits awkwardly with an open-ended payment stream and an unfixed closing date. That is a mild but real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary headings-are-not-substantive boilerplate; nothing to construe. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision depends on a heading for its meaning, so there is nothing to conflict with. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Singular/plural and gender boilerplate; no ambiguity available. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It does not interact operatively with any other clause. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The laws of the state in which the Property is located' is determinate (Michigan) even though it does not name the state, and successors/'permitted assigns' is standard. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision of the Agreement grants or restricts assignment, so 'permitted assigns' has no referent here, and §24 contemplates an assignment from GSA to Buyer under a separate Option; a federal-agency-related buyer also sits oddly with a state-law-only clause. Modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Prevailing party, as determined by the court in such action' supplies its own decision rule, which removes most of the usual argument. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against §10, which lists specific-performance and damages remedies plus 'any other remedy available at law or in equity' — fee-shifting is additive rather than contradictory. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short sentences requiring writing and signature by 'each party hereto', with counterpart execution permitted; nothing internally ambiguous. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §24 says the Agreement 'may be amended only by written instrument, executed by the Buyer, Seller and the Government, acting by GSA' — the Government is not a party hereto, so §22 and §24 prescribe different signature sets for the same act. That is a direct conflict between two operative provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The survival period is defined by events outside the sale — 'until fulfilled, up to and including the time of completion of any improvements to be built thereon and the written acceptance of occupancy... by GSA' — which is indefinite and assumes a construction and lease that this Agreement does not provide for. 'Until fulfilled' and the GSA occupancy trigger are namable vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with §7's closing sentence (representations true 'on each day hereafter'), §6 (as-is acceptance) and §24 (entire agreement limited to this Agreement and the Option), the survival period keys off events governed by neither instrument. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause first says the Agreement 'cancels and supersedes all prior agreements' and 'is entire in itself', then says this Agreement and the August 2006 Option 'are the only agreements' — a merger clause that both excludes and preserves a prior instrument, with the Option's date left blank. That internal push-pull, plus 'No promises... other than those expressly contained herein', is squarely construable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts with §22 (amendment by 'each party hereto') by requiring the Government's signature, and §3 depends on the preserved Option Agreement to supply the 'Permitted Exceptions', so the superseded/preserved status of the Option matters operatively. Named conflicts with §22 and §3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line recording prohibition with no qualifiers and no remedy stated; nothing to construe on its face. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere gives Buyer a right to record or a memorandum of option, so no conflict appears; §24's preserved Option is a separate instrument. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence makes Buyer solely responsible for all utility 'terminations, and relocations' costs 'after 8 closing' — a stray page number breaking the text — and 'public and quasi-public and private' utilities is an untidy catch-all. The garbled timing phrase is a mechanical defect that bears on when the cost shift begins.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its first sentence duplicates §7(c) but adds 'Gas' and drops the qualifier 'for its current use', so the same representation appears twice in materially different words; §9 also allocates 'expenses and charges in connection with ownership and use'. That divergence from §7(c) is a specific inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary counterparts boilerplate; no competing readings available. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: §22 separately permits amendments in counterparts, which is duplicative but consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Cooperate... to secure all necessary government approvals for an approved Brownfield Plan and any other applicable grant and/or loan programs' is an unbounded catch-all after a specific item, and 'cooperate' states no standard of effort. Both are namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its last sentence repeats §2's closing sentence almost verbatim but substitutes 'less any setoff' for 'less any deductions', and the whole TIF payment engine in §2 depends on a Brownfield Plan that this clause treats only as an object of cooperation, not a condition. The §2 divergence is a concrete inconsistency.
